newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to continue selling GM Cavalier.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to continue selling GM Cavalier.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday it planned to continue sales in Japan of the Cavalier, a model based on General Motors Corp's (GM)Chevrolet Cavalier, despite poor demand.

"We will continue sales of Cavaliers in Japan. We have not reached the stage yet of giving up, despite failing to achieve the expected 20,000 units," Toyota executive vice-president Akira Yokoi told Reuters in an interview.
Sales in Japan of GM-made Toyota Cavaliers totalled 11,407 units in calendar 1996. Toyota started selling the model in Japan in January 1996 with an annual sales target of 20,000 units.
"Toyota and GM know we must try to boost sales of Cavaliers in Japan. Toyota will ask GM to improve the cars to make them more attractive to Japanese tastes," Yokoi said.

In April Toyota conducted a sales campaign offering 100 one million yen coupons exchangeable for accessories to customers who bought Cavaliers that month. The model is priced at between 1.81 million yen and 2.05 million yen in Japan.

Toyota and GM agreed in November 1993 that Toyota would market GM cars under the Toyota brand name, amid strong pressure from the U.S. government for measures to boost sales of American cars in Japan. ($1=116 yen)
